title: Pre-Analysis — Residual Fleet Position for the Corrosion-Resistant Latch Hook Standard
abstract: Work order raised to price a residual embodiment campaign for the first-generation corrosion-resistant latch hook set, cancelled once the analysis showed the remaining aircraft should be taken directly to the load-sharing carriage standard instead.

sections.objective: Establish whether a residual embodiment campaign for the corrosion-resistant latch hook set is worth launching for the aircraft that never took it, following the line-check wear reports that arrived through the operator order this spring. The work order had to quantify the remaining unmodified population, confirm that the hook set is still procurable, and check what the later latching standards do to the case before any campaign was priced.
sections.findings_summary: The analysis did not survive contact with the supersession record. The load-sharing hook and roller arrangement supersedes this standard outright and its own retrofit vehicle is already open, so an aircraft taken to the first-generation hook set would have to be opened a second time within the same inspection interval. The parts figure confirms the two hook sets are not interchangeable and that the earlier item is now spares-only. The web fretting repair, which most of the remaining aircraft carry, is written against the later carriage geometry and would have to be re-substantiated for the earlier hook seat. On that basis the work order was cancelled rather than completed, and the residual population was folded into the later campaign.
sections.next_steps: Close the residual campaign question and record the position against the operator order so that the same request does not return. Ask the door design authority to state the remaining population against the load-sharing standard instead, and to confirm that the spares-only status of the earlier hook set is reflected in the illustrated parts data. No further pre-analysis effort is warranted on this modification; the sealed bearing cartridge candidate now carries the subject.

Assess approved repairs carried by the residual population

evidence.similarity_note: Reached directly from the supersession edge and confirmed by the shared door zone and chapter; the hook part numbers themselves are disjoint because the later standard replaced all of them.

expected_findings.rationale: The load-sharing hook and roller arrangement supersedes this standard and its retrofit vehicle is already available to the same population. Embodying the earlier hook set now would require the door to be opened twice inside one inspection interval for no residual benefit.
expected_findings.resolution: Cancel the residual campaign and transfer the remaining population to the later standard.

expected_findings.rationale: The figure carries both hook sets and marks the earlier one as not interchangeable with the later carriage arrangement, with spares provisioning already run down. A campaign would need a new procurement case that nobody has raised.
expected_findings.resolution: Confirm the spares-only status is correctly reflected and leave the figure unchanged.

expected_findings.rationale: Most of the residual aircraft carry the hook seat fretting repair on the latching web. That repair was substantiated against the later carriage geometry and its hook seat contact pattern; putting the earlier hook back onto a repaired web would need its own substantiation.
expected_findings.resolution: No action, the campaign is cancelled. Record the constraint in case the question returns.

expected_non_findings.reason: Returned by every latching search and shares the door zones and chapter, but it is a wear survey and baseline record with no embodiment content. It neither competes with nor prevents a hook set campaign and was correctly set aside.

type_data.conclusion: Work order cancelled after the supersession position became clear. The residual population is transferred to the later latching standard; no campaign will be priced against this modification.
